subject: PHI/PII preservation exceptions and selective scrub options — scenario Q&A
messages:
From: Danielle Byrne <danielle.byrne@stclaire-health.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@stclaire-health.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on retention exceptions and scrub options for high-risk PHI

Marissa —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Before we proceed to contract, our legal and privacy teams had a couple of scenario-driven questions around retention and deletion:

1) For clinical transcripts (full visit notes) — can you support a preservation exception where a subset of records is held for 7 years for compliance while others are purged on a 1-year cadence? How would that map to Redwood retention policies and any indexing/cache artifacts?

2) If we ask Redwood to "redact" SSNs and patient names, what options do we have that keep downstream embeddings usable for routing but remove cleartext identifiers? E.g., pseudonymization vs deterministic tokenization vs full masking.

3) When we issue an erasure request for a patient, how quickly can you scrub cached KV state and any transient inference artifacts? Is there an audit trail for the purge action?

Can you share a short matrix that maps each scrub approach to: post-scrub usability (search/semantic match), latency impact, and estimated cost delta?

Appreciate it — Danielle
St. Claire Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Byrne <danielle.byrne@stclaire-health.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Questions on retention exceptions and scrub options for high-risk PHI

Danielle —

Thanks for the clear scenarios. Looping in Rishi (security/compliance) and Priyom (solutions) so we can answer with specifics and a short options matrix. High level answers below; we'll follow up with the matrix PDF and a CSV mapping example by EOD.

- Preservation exceptions: yes, Redwood supports per-tenant and per-record retention policies. We surface retention windows at the document slice level, and you can tag sets for longer retention (e.g., 7y) while setting defaults at 1y. Important caveat: indexes and some inference caches (prefix caches, semantic indexes used for retrieval-augmented workflows) may retain derived vectors unless you explicitly request purge of derived artifacts; we describe purge scopes in the matrix.

- Redaction/pseudonymization options: we support three common strategies: full masking (remove and replace with [REDACTED]), deterministic pseudonymization (consistent tokens like Patient_#### to preserve referential joins), and reversible tokenization via KMS-backed token vault (reversible but access-controlled). Deterministic pseudonymization preserves semantic similarity better than full masking. Reversible tokenization preserves maximum utility but raises key management requirements.

- Erasure SLOs: for typical requests we can purge primary documents within 24-72 hours; derived artifacts (embeddings, cache shards) are targeted within 3–10 business days depending on index size and shard compaction schedules. All purge actions are logged and we can provide an exportable audit record (timestamp, actor, scope).

Rishi/Priyom — can you attach the scrub-options matrix and an example retention-exceptions CSV?

— Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Danielle Byrne <danielle.byrne@stclaire-health.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Questions on retention exceptions and scrub options for high-risk PHI

Danielle / team —

Adding security detail and the matrix. Attached "field-scrub-options-matrix.pdf" covers tradeoffs at a glance. Key notes:

* Preservation exceptions: our retention engine supports record-level tags and retention inheritance. Preserved records are isolated from automated purge jobs and are excluded from compaction windows unless an admin removes the tag. We also snapshot indexing pointers so you can opt into preserving search references for preserved records or force pointer removal (tradeoff: searchability).

* Embeddings/Derived artifacts: we mark derived vectors with parent IDs and maintain a separate derived-object store. On a purge we perform a cascade delete: primary -> derived -> cache shards -> index segments. Immediate removal of primary content is fast; derived-object GC is asynchronous to avoid impacting hot-path latency. We provide a purge job status and final confirmation.

* Scrub approaches (high level):
  - Full masking: zero risk of identifier leakage; search/semantic matching is degraded. Low implementation cost.
  - Deterministic pseudonymization: consistent mappings preserve cross-document joins and reasonable semantic matching; low risk if mapping stored client-side or in an HSM-backed store.
  - Token vault (reversible): best utility for downstream models and retrieval; requires KMS/HSM and strict access controls — higher compliance burden.

SLO examples:
  - Single-record erasure (no derived index): target 24h
  - Indexed cohorts (10k records): 3–5 business days (index compaction scheduling)
  - Large-scale cohort purge (100k+): 7–10 business days with incremental compaction windows

Attachments included: field-scrub-options-matrix.pdf, data-retention-exceptions-table.csv

Rishi Malhotra
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Questions on retention exceptions and scrub options for high-risk PHI

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple quick follow-ups:

1) If we elect deterministic pseudonymization, can Redwood expose the pseudonym mapping via a customer-managed HSM so that only our systems can resolve tokens back to PHI? We prefer reversible only behind our keys.

2) For audit purposes, will the purge logs include the list of object IDs removed and a checksum? Procurement would like that to satisfy an internal SOC-type workflow.

3) Pricing: for preserved records outside the default 1-year window, is there a premium (we expect ~8% of our corpus to be flagged for 7-year retention)? If so, how is the premium calculated (GB-months? index footprint?)

If you can reply with short bullets, we can decide whether to push for a 7y exception in the MSA.

— Danielle

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Byrne <danielle.byrne@stclaire-health.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-21T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Questions on retention exceptions and scrub options for high-risk PHI

Danielle — quick bullets addressing your follow-ups: 

- HSM-backed pseudonym mapping: yes. We can store mapping keys in a customer-controlled KMS/HSM and encrypt mapping metadata such that only your KMS can decrypt. That satisfies the reversible-only-behind-your-keys requirement. Implementation requires a one-off key integration and small onboarding runbook (we'll attach the runbook link).

- Purge logs: we include object IDs, timestamps, actor, scope (primary vs derived), and SHA256 checksums for primary objects. Confirmations can be exported as CSV or uploaded to your secure S3.

- Pricing for preserved records: there is a preservation premium calculated on preserved GB-months plus an index-residency surcharge. For a sample: 8% of corpus preserved => incremental charge equals (preserved GB-months * preservation rate) + (index residency surcharge applied per index shard per month). We'll share a tailored estimate once you provide expected GBs and index count.

Attached: sample preservation-cost-calculation.csv and a short onboarding runbook link. Let us know if you want us to draft MSA language for a 7y exception.

— Priyom
Solutions — Redwood Inference
